newsitem.title: EGYPT: Jordan crown prince, Mubarak discuss peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Jordan crown prince, Mubarak discuss peace crisis.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan arrived in Egypt on Thursday and met President Hosni Mubarak for talks on the latest crisis in the Middle East peace process that was set off by twin suicide bombings in Jerusalem.
Officials said the two men were meeting privately first and would later be joined by the prime ministers and foreign ministers of both countries.
Egypt and Jordan, the only two Arab states which have peace deals with Israel, have led diplomatic efforts to ease the latest crisis ahead of a visit to the region by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross.

Prince Hassan proved unable in talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Wednesday to persuade Israel to ease sanctions imposed after the bombings in a Jerusalem market last week.
The explosions killed 15 people, including the two bombers, in the deadliest attack against Israelis in a year.

In the aftermath, Israel suspended a resumption of its talks with the Palestinians and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, preventing Palestinians from going to their places of work in Israel proper.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was quoted on Thursday as saying measures imposed by Israel against the Palestinians since the bombings amounted to a declaration of war.
"Netanyahu has declared war on us and we have to prepare for what will come. The situation is serious," Arafat was quoted as saying in an interview with the Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth.

Mubarak, who met Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Cairo on Tuesday called on Israel to ease the sanctions against the Palestinians and said the Jewish state should resume peace talks despite attacks.
